lane: OW-3 bounded re-adjudication (post-feedback; the OW-2 item-1 baseline is preserved)

queue_items.claim: The row states no tier-1 signal at its own front seam and never engages the preceding verse's bytes.
queue_items.grounds: The whole front-seam argument is 'A finite third-person-plural clause, “They will rebuild the old ruins.” (web:Isa.61.4), matching וּבָנוּ֙ חָרְב֣וֹת עוֹלָ֔ם (oshb:Isa.61.4, byte tier), opens a report of the community's restoration' — an assertion that the clause opens a unit, with no stated reason why it does. MT 61:3 is never quoted, never named and carries no entry in boundary_evidence_refs, yet its own close is a finite waw-plus-perfect clause too, וְקֹרָ֤א לָהֶם֙ אֵילֵ֣י הַצֶּ֔דֶק מַטַּ֥ע יְהוָ֖ה לְהִתְפָּאֵֽר (oshb:Isa.61.3, byte tier), so the cited construction does not discriminate the seam. No vocative, imperative onset, messenger frame, wayyiqtol onset or addressee change stands at MT 61:4, and no parashah mark falls at this seam in the inventory.
queue_items.proposed_change: Field repair (no seam movement): argue the front seam against MT 61:3's own bytes — the first-person commissioned-speaker frame closing there versus the subjectless third-person restoration report opening at MT 61:4 — and add oshb:Isa.61.3 to boundary_evidence_refs; observed_substrate_signals, rejected_alternative and confidence are dependent fields of the added driver.

prior_adjudication.grounds: The shipped row's front-seam sentence asserts that וּבָנוּ֙ חָרְב֣וֹת עוֹלָ֔ם (oshb:Isa.61.4, byte tier) 'opens a report' and gives no reason it opens a unit; boundary_evidence_refs carries neither oshb:Isa.61.3 nor web:Isa.61.3, and MT 61:3 is never quoted or named. Re-derived: MT 61:3 closes on the finite waw-plus-perfect clause וְקֹרָ֤א לָהֶם֙ אֵילֵ֣י הַצֶּ֔דֶק מַטַּ֥ע יְהוָ֖ה לְהִתְפָּאֵֽר (oshb:Isa.61.3, byte tier), so 'a finite third-person-plural clause' does not by itself discriminate 61:4 from the verse before it; MT 61:4, וּבָנוּ֙ חָרְב֣וֹת עוֹלָ֔ם שֹׁמְמ֥וֹת רִֽאשֹׁנִ֖ים יְקוֹמֵ֑מוּ וְחִדְּשׁוּ֙ עָ֣רֵי חֹ֔רֶב שֹׁמְמ֖וֹת דּ֥וֹר וָדֽוֹר (oshb:Isa.61.4, byte tier), carries no vocative, imperative, messenger formula, wayyiqtol or explicit addressee change; and the mark inventory keys no seg at 61:4 and only a count-only paseq at 61:3, the nearest SAMEKH segs being keyed at 60:22 and 61:9. The seam itself survives on a ground this row never states: the commissioned speaker's first-person forms עָלָ֑י, אֹתִ֜י and שְׁלָחַ֨נִי֙ (oshb:Isa.61.1, byte tier) and the purpose infinitives they govern end at 61:3, and nothing in 61:4-61:9 resumes that voice (the plural suffix on אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ (oshb:Isa.61.6, byte tier) and the divine first person אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ (oshb:Isa.61.8, byte tier) are distinct objects). A load-bearing seam with no stated warrant in its own row, held by a byte-sound ground available to the pair, is a warrant defect and not a disclosure gap: medium as filed. The proposed repair (argue the seam against MT 61:3's bytes, add oshb:Isa.61.3, treat observed_substrate_signals, rejected_alternative and confidence as dependent fields) stands with no seam movement.

queue_items.readjudication_instruction: Apply the both-sides seam law: weigh the adjacent unit's close (for a front seam) or onset (for a rear seam) from bytes BEFORE ruling; if the filed finding's ground was onset-only, re-rule on the complete test under the strategy (§6: refrains close units; frame onsets; addressee shifts; imperative/vocative summons; formula onsets).

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: A finite third-person-plural clause, “They will rebuild the old ruins.” (web:Isa.61.4), matching וּבָנוּ֙ חָרְב֣וֹת עוֹלָ֔ם (oshb:Isa.61.4, byte tier), opens a report of the community's restoration that continues through an explicit address shift, “But you will be called Yahweh's priests.” (web:Isa.61.6), matching וְאַתֶּ֗ם כֹּהֲנֵ֤י יְהוָה֙ תִּקָּרֵ֔אוּ (oshb:Isa.61.6, byte tier), and a first-person divine declaration, “For I, Yahweh, love justice.” (web:Isa.61.8), matching כִּ֣י אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ אֹהֵ֣ב מִשְׁפָּ֔ט (oshb:Isa.61.8, byte tier), none of these bringing a vocative or scene marker distinct from the same covenant promise. The unit closes on the blessed-offspring report, “that they are the offspring which Yahweh has blessed.” (web:Isa.61.9), before Isa.61.10 opens with a fresh first-person voice, “I will greatly rejoice in Yahweh!” (web:Isa.61.10), sharing no stated referent with the third-person offspring just named.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting a boundary at Isa.61.6's shift to second-person-plural address was rejected because no vocative, imperative onset, or explicit scene change accompanies the pronoun shift, and the same covenant promise continues in the same voice through Isa.61.9.
shipped_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
shipped_row.device_notes: A setumah (single-witness) marks oshb:Isa.61.9 at this unit's own close, tier-3 corroboration. The internal shift from third-person 'they' to second-person-plural 'you' at Isa.61.6 and to first-person 'I, Yahweh' at Isa.61.8 is read as in-unit texture rather than a boundary driver, since the three shifts lack a vocative, imperative onset, or massa/hoy/koh-amar frame of their own.

prev_row.boundary_rationale: A first-person speaker announces a commission, “The Lord Yahweh's Spirit is on me, because Yahweh has anointed me to preach good news to the humble.” (web:Isa.61.1), matching ר֛וּחַ אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה עָלָ֑י (oshb:Isa.61.1, byte tier). A chain of purpose infinitives governed by that same sending — to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty and release, to comfort mourners, to give a garland for ashes — runs to the verse's own caesura at כֵּהָ֑ה (oshb:Isa.61.3, byte tier) and continues, not as a further infinitive but as a waw-plus-perfect finite clause naming the mourners themselves as its subject, וְקֹרָ֤א לָהֶם֙ (oshb:Isa.61.3, byte tier): “that they may be called trees of righteousness, the planting of Yahweh, that he may be glorified.” (web:Isa.61.3), matching מַטַּ֥ע יְהוָ֖ה לְהִתְפָּאֵֽר (oshb:Isa.61.3, byte tier). Isa.61.4 opens a further waw-plus-perfect clause with a changed subject, “They will rebuild the old ruins.” (web:Isa.61.4) — the third-person-plural community now rebuilding, distinct from the mourners just named and called a planting at the unit's own close — marking this unit's close.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Reading the first-person mission statement as continuing through Isa.61.4's building report was rejected because the infinitive-purpose chain governed by Yahweh's sending closes at Isa.61.3's own glorification clause, and Isa.61.4 opens a new finite-verb clause with a third-person-plural subject. Labeling the unit servant_song was considered and set aside because this unit's own bytes lack the eved-root vocabulary that anchors the book's servant census, leaving the anointed speaker's identity an open question the unit does not resolve.
prev_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
prev_row.device_notes: A setumah (single-witness) at oshb:Isa.60.22 closes the preceding unit immediately before this one opens; a paseq (single-witness, count-only, no intra-verse position asserted) sits at oshb:Isa.61.3, inside this unit's own span. The catchword closing this unit is tier-mixed, not uniformly byte-true: the 'to be glorified' verb is byte-identical between the two units, לְהִתְפָּאֵֽר (oshb:Isa.60.21, byte tier) and לְהִתְפָּאֵֽר (oshb:Isa.61.3, byte tier), but the paired planting noun is not — oshb:Isa.60.21 stages the ketiv/qere pair מטעו מַטָּעַ֛י (unpointed ketiv beside pointed qere) against this unit's own מַטַּ֥ע (oshb:Isa.61.3, byte tier), the two meeting only at skeleton tier (sweep: 3 verses book-wide on that consonantal string). This tier-mixed catchword is disclosed here rather than treated as evidence against the boundary already argued from the subject shift at Isa.61.4. Labeling this unit servant_song was weighed and set aside: this unit's own bytes (Isa.61.1-Isa.61.3) lack the eved-root servant vocabulary that anchors the book's own servant census, so the identity of the anointed first-person speaker stays an open question this unit does not resolve.

next_row.boundary_rationale: A new first-person voice opens with rejoicing, “I will greatly rejoice in Yahweh! My soul will be joyful in my God,” (web:Isa.61.10), matching שׂ֧וֹשׂ אָשִׂ֣ישׂ בַּֽיהוָ֗ה (oshb:Isa.61.10, byte tier), sharing no stated referent with the third-person 'offspring' of the immediately preceding report. The bridegroom-and-bride simile carries the same voice through a comparison to Adonai Yahweh's own action, “so the Lord Yahweh will cause righteousness and praise to spring up before all the nations.” (web:Isa.61.11), matching אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה (oshb:Isa.61.11, byte tier). Isa.62.1 opens a distinct first-person resolve, “For Zion's sake I will not hold my peace, and for Jerusalem's sake I will not rest,” (web:Isa.62.1); the first-person-singular voice itself runs on unbroken from this unit's own opening rejoicing into that vow, so the seam is marked by the shift in rhetorical mode — from a sung report of what Yahweh has already done to a vow of what the speaker will now do — rather than by any change in speaker or person, closing this unit.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating Isa.61.10-Isa.61.11 as a continuation of the restoration promise closing at Isa.61.9 was rejected because the abrupt shift from third-person description of 'their offspring' to a first-person 'I will greatly rejoice' introduces a new speaking voice without a stated referent.
next_row.wj_or_red_letter_considered: not applicable in the OT substrate
next_row.device_notes: A setumah (single-witness) at oshb:Isa.61.9 marks the front seam immediately before this unit opens; a paseq (single-witness, count-only, no intra-verse position asserted) sits at oshb:Isa.61.11, inside this unit's own close. This unit's own opening simile reuses, at accent_stripped tier, the garland word that closes the anointed speaker's commission three verses earlier: פְּאֵ֜ר (oshb:Isa.61.3, byte tier) against פְּאֵ֔ר (oshb:Isa.61.10, byte tier) differ only in cantillation; the standalone token stands in exactly 2 verses book-wide. This is disclosed continuity across this unit's own front seam, and it does not resolve whether the rejoicing voice is the same figure who speaks beginning at Isa.61.1. Labeling this two-verse unit hymn_doxology extends the operative category beyond the strategy's own enumerated song sites, by the sung first-person praise content of its own bytes; the speaking voice — Zion personified, or the same figure who speaks beginning at Isa.61.1 — is left open rather than decided here.
